server_url.help: Base URL of your ntfy server. Defaults to https://ntfy.sh — change to your self-hosted instance (e.g. https://ntfy.example.com) for on-prem setups.

topic.help: Topic name subscribers receive on the ntfy app. Use a unique name (e.g. mcharbor-alerts-prod). ntfy.sh allows up to 64 chars of [a-zA-Z0-9_-].

access_token.help: Topic-scoped token from ntfy. Click 'Get token' on the topic page in the ntfy web UI. Takes precedence over username/password when set. Encrypted at rest.

priority.help: Optional. One of min, low, default, high, urgent. Maps to ntfy's integer priority 1/2/3/4/5. Leave blank for server default.

tags.help: Optional. Comma-separated emoji shortcodes rendered as inline icons in the ntfy mobile app (e.g. 'warning,rocket'). See https://docs.ntfy.sh/emojis/ for the catalog.

page.title: ntfys
page.subtitle: Route workflow, alert, and backup events to an ntfy topic via HTTP POST. The plugin handles Test (publishes a real test message) and Send (publishes Title + Message as the body) — there is no OAuth flow because ntfy uses static topic tokens or HTTP Basic auth.
page.registerHint: Add a channel from the host's Notifications > Channels page and pick "ntfy" as the channel_type.

error.noTopic: Topic is required. Set the topic name subscribers will receive alerts on.

form.publishBody: ntfy is a pub/sub HTTP service. The plugin POSTs the notification Title as the `Title` header and the Message as the request body to `<server_url>/<topic>`. Subscribers receive it in the ntfy Android/iOS/web app immediately. Click **Save**, then **Test connection** to verify the topic + credentials round-trip a real publish.
form.authToken: **Access Token** — preferred. Topic-scoped token from the ntfy web UI under topic settings. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Each topic gets its own token so revoking one doesn't break the others.
form.authBasic: **Username + Password** — for self-hosted ntfy with per-user auth. Sent as HTTP Basic. Only used when Access Token is blank.
form.authNone: **Neither** — fine for public topics on ntfy.sh. Anyone with the topic name can publish, so pick a long unguessable name for production alerts.
form.priorityBody: Set Priority to **high** or **urgent** to bypass Do Not Disturb on iOS and Android. ntfy maps urgent (5) to the phone's alarm-stream volume on Android — use sparingly. Tags are inline icons in the mobile app; pick one or two shortcodes per channel type (e.g. `warning` for alerts, `rocket` for backup-complete) so subscribers can scan the topic visually.
form.testBody: The Test call publishes a real message (`Title: McHarbor test notification`, body `McHarbor test notification`) to your topic. The ntfy server returns 200 OK on success; the plugin translates any non-2xx into a structured error showing the upstream status code + first 256 bytes of the server's JSON error body. Subscribers will see the test message — let them know before clicking Test so it doesn't generate a false-positive alert ticket.

step1.body: Decide where your alerts go: ntfy.sh (cloud, free, public topics only by default) or self-hosted ntfy (Docker image, full control over auth and topic privacy). Set Server URL accordingly — leave it blank for ntfy.sh.

step2.body: Pick a topic name. ntfy.sh allows up to 64 chars of [a-zA-Z0-9_-]. Use a unique name per environment (e.g. mcharbor-alerts-prod, mcharbor-alerts-staging) so subscribers can mute one without losing the other. The topic name itself is the publish endpoint, so don't put secrets in it.

step3.body: Subscribe on the receiving device: install the ntfy Android or iOS app (or visit ntfy.sh in a browser) and tap + to add a topic. Type the exact same name you used in step 2. Without a subscriber on this device, your alerts go nowhere.

step4.body: For ntfy.sh: open the topic in the web UI, click the lock icon, and generate a topic-scoped access token. Paste it into the Access Token field on the left. Cloud topics are publicly readable unless you check the "authenticated users only" box — token-protected publishes are still public-read by default, so the token stops random internet users from injecting messages, not from reading them.

step5.body: For self-hosted ntfy: fill in Username + Password for HTTP Basic auth (set in the ntfy config under auth-default-access). The plugin uses Bearer token if Access Token is set, falls back to Basic when only username + password are present. Both is treated as "token wins".

step6.body: Optional: set Priority to high or urgent to bypass Do Not Disturb. urgent maps to ntfy's integer 5 — Android renders it on the alarm stream, iOS pre-empts silent mode. Use for downtime / backup-failure alerts only.

step7.body: Optional: add Tags as a comma-separated list of emoji shortcodes (e.g. "warning,rocket") — the ntfy mobile app renders these as inline icons next to each message. Browse the catalog at https://docs.ntfy.sh/emojis/.

step8.body: Save the channel. Click Test connection — the plugin publishes "McHarbor test notification" to your topic. Your subscriber device should receive it within 1-2 seconds. If Test returns 401, the access token is wrong; if 404, the topic name doesn't match what subscribers added; if 429, ntfy.sh rate-limited the publish (5 messages per 10s per topic on the free tier).

step9.body: Once the channel is saved, route workflow or alert events to it from Settings > Notifications > Rules. ntfy delivery is fire-and-forget: a failed publish is logged in the audit log and surfaced in the host toast, but the host does not retry.
